what_this_file_is: Halloween 2026 - the list of games. THE ONE PLACE to add, rename, reorder or describe a game.
The app reads this file when it starts and makes one button per game in the bottom panel.
Add a game: put its files in games/<folder_name>/ (with an index.html inside) and add an entry above.
Nothing in app/ ever changes. app.js reads this file; a game designer never edits app.js.
What goes here: anything the player might want while BROWSING games, before tapping one.
Also here: up to three simple on/off switches for your game (see settings below), which the app draws and remembers for you.
Everything else (assets, sizes, any options screen of your own) lives in the game's own folder; the app never reads it.
If the same fact is in both places, this file wins: the app shows what is written here.
JSON cannot hold comments, which is why this _about block exists. The app ignores it.
It sits at the bottom so the data comes first.

fields.folder_name: The game's folder under games/. LOWERCASE ONLY (GitHub Pages is case-sensitive). Required.
fields.goes_in_slot: Where the game appears: a whole number 1 to 8 for a fixed cell on the button board. The game in slot 1 is also the one shown when the app starts (behind the open GAMES tab). The board is two rows of four: 1 2 3 4 across the upper row, 5 6 7 8 across the lower row. A game always sits in its own cell, so slot 1 is always top left and slot 8 always bottom right; cells nobody uses stay empty. If only one row has games, that row is drawn in the middle. 9 or above, or "", means the game is listed but not shown - an easy way to bench a game. If two entries claim the same slot, the first one in the file wins.
fields.title: The game's full name, shown in the THIS GAME tab (and on the button when there is no usable icon). May use the text marks described under description, including "\n" for a second, smaller line in the tab when the game's own look asks for it; the button's spoken name uses the plain words.
fields.short_title: A short name shown in the narrow top bar, and on the button when there is no usable icon (the button fits about ten characters per line, two lines). About 12 characters is comfortable; the bar holds about 24 on the smallest phone and cuts anything longer with an ellipsis. May use the marks: an __accent__ is orange in the top bar, the rest white. Leave it the same as title if the title is short.
fields.icon: Path to the game's icon, relative to the game's folder, e.g. assets/icon.png. SPEC: a square 256 x 256 real pixels, PNG with a transparent background (or an SVG with a square viewBox). Draw anything that fills the square; it is shown inside an orange rounded button with a small orange margin, so plan for orange around it. Wiggle room: each side may be 200 to 300 pixels and the two sides may differ by up to 10; the app scales it. Outside that, or missing, or a bad path: the button shows short_title as text instead (and says why in the browser console).
fields.designer: Who made the game. Free text.
fields.credits: Where art, sound or ideas came from. Free text, may be empty.
fields.date: When the game was finished or last changed. Free text, for display only.
fields.description: One or two sentences about the game, shown in the THIS GAME tab. One string, or a list of strings shown as separate paragraphs. Marks understood: **bold**, __accent__ (the game's accent style; bold unless styles.css section 5b says more), ~~rainbow~~ (a colour per letter), "\n" for a new line inside a paragraph, and a paragraph starting with "!! " for a shaded emphasis line. No HTML.
fields.how_to_play: Short instructions, shown in the THIS GAME tab. One string, or a list of strings shown as separate paragraphs, with the same marks as description. Keep it to a few sentences.
fields.settings: Optional: up to three on/off switches for your game, shown in the THIS GAME tab next to the high scores. (There is no app-wide Sound switch any more; sound is your game's own job.) A list of { "label": "Easy / Hard", "default": 0 } entries. The switch's left position is 0 and its right position is 1, so a label written as "Left / Right" lines up with the switch. Keep a label to about 20 characters. default is where the switch starts (0 or 1); after that the app remembers each player's choice on their own device. [] or no settings field = no switches of your own. A fourth entry is ignored. AS THINGS STAND the switches are only shown and remembered: no game can read them, so they change nothing in a game. A setting your game really needs is your game's own job (its own options screen, say).

good_to_know: High scores need nothing in this file: a game includes games/game-helper.js and calls Halloween.reportScore(42) at game over; the app keeps the five best per game on the player's device and shows them in the THIS GAME tab. A game may add up to two short notes to a score, such as the opponent or the variant: Halloween.reportScore(3, "3-2", ["vs. Ron", "3 set game"]). See the top of games/game-helper.js.

High scores need nothing in this file: a game includes games/game-helper.js and calls Halloween.reportScore(42) at game over; the app keeps the five best per game on the player's device and shows them in the THIS GAME tab. See the top of games/game-helper.js.

The app never pauses a game. The player can open the bottom panel at any time, it covers about the lower half of the game, and the game is not paused or told. A game that needs a pause builds its own. See 1.8 in games/README - game design requirements.md.

A game may have its THIS GAME tab drawn in its own style: app.js puts the class look-<folder_name> on the tab, and section 5b of app/styles.css may hold rules for it (Candy Go Fish does this). Ask before adding yours; a game without rules there looks like the others.
